messages:
mia: Heads up — after canary of kernel-selector v2 we saw ~12% p99 latency regression on seq_len>=1024 traffic :thinking:
alex: which pool/region? can you drop the perf numbers + a flame/profile?
mia: canary is us-west-2 gpu-pool-3 (10% traffic). quick numbers from probe windows:
```
kernel-selector:v2 (canary)
p50: 28ms
p95: 120ms (+8% vs v1)
p99: 320ms (+12% vs v1)
workload: tail-heavy, seq_len bins >=1024 dominate
kv_hit_rate: 18% -> 7% after deploy
trace: hot path moves from fused-attn-fp16 -> generic-gemm fallback on some shards
```
deploy-bot: Deploy kernel-selector:v2 -> canary(10%) completed at 2026-03-15T18:33Z :shipit:
alex: kv_hit drop is suspicious — did keying change or driver build tag differ?
mia: I compared keys in logs. observed driver_build changed and we have a driver tag appended to keys now on v2. example log snippets:
```
cache_key=bert|v3|khash=ab12|seq_bin=1024-2048|driver=driver-20260315-rc2
cache_key_prev=bert|v3|khash=ab12|seq_bin=1024-2048|driver=driver-20260308
```
kevin: that's it — driver tag in key means older entries become unreachable => cold starts. Not a correctness bug but a retention/migration design gap.
sanjay: two quick options: 1) include a driver-agnostic alias lookup layer (key -> canonical_key) 2) make key include driver_sha but have background rewarm that rewrites hot entries after deploy.
julia: rewarm sounds reasonable. For large fleets we should avoid duplicate persistent entries across builds (storage blowup). propose: mark keys with driver_tag but keep tombstone alias for N days and lazy-rewrite hot prefixes.
ops: fyi storage for kv-store is metered; doubling keys for a week could be expensive. need estimate if we go lazy-rewrite + keep tombstone for 72h.
alex: also consider adding kernel_selector_version and quant_profile to key to avoid semantic collisions when kernel picks change behavior. sample proposed schema:
```
kv_key = f"{model_id}|{model_version}|{kernel_hash}|{seq_bin}|{kernel_selector_sha}|{driver_build}"
```
mia: if we add kernel_selector_sha we should also update persistence so old keys are still useful for reads during migration. I suggest a read-fallback policy: try full key then fallback to key without driver_build then fallback to kernel-less key for last resort.
kevin: agreed. fallback order reduces misses but increases lookup ops. we'll need metrics by fallback-step.
sanjay: TTL heuristics: shorter TTL for cross-driver duplicates, increment hot-score on cache-hit, background_rewrite triggers when hot-score > threshold. Also keep per-key last_validated_build to avoid thrashing.
julia: migration sequence I propose:
1) roll key-schema change server-side but keep read-fallback logic
2) deploy rewarm workers that scan hot prefixes and rewrite to new key namespace lazily
3) emit metrics kv_miss_by_driver and kv_fallback_rates
4) after N days and stable hit-rates, garbage collect old keys
kevin: add CI perf-tests for seq_len bins >=512/1024 to catch regressions before rollout. baseline p99 targets: <= +3% vs current for canary.
mia: action items:
- [ ] rollback if p99 > +10% sustained for 30m
- [x] add kernel_selector_sha to key schema in code (server side guarded)
- [ ] implement read-fallback (full -> drop-driver -> drop-kernel)
- [ ] start background rewarm job with hot-score threshold
- [ ] add metrics: kv_miss_by_driver, kv_fallback_rate, kv_dup_storage_bytes
- [ ] add perf CI for seq_len heavy workloads (ci-bot)
ci-bot: perf-run triggered: suite=seqlen-heavy p95/p99 profiles queued :gear:
ops: please provide storage cost estimate for tombstone period (72h) before full rollout.
alex: I'll pair with @mia tomorrow to draft read-fallback PR and perf tests.
mia: thanks — I'll attach flame graphs and more traces to the PR. low-friction rollback plan ready. :white_check_mark: :rocket:
